text: Then Naomi, her mother-in-law, said to her, "My daughter, should I not look for a home for you, where you will be well provided for?
Now Boaz, whose young women you have worked with, is a relative of ours. Tonight he will be winnowing barley at the threshing floor.
So wash and anoint yourself, put on your best clothes, and go down to the threshing floor. But do not let him know you are there until he has finished eating and drinking.
When he lies down, note the place where he lies. Then go, uncover his feet, and lie down. He will tell you what to do."
"I will do everything you say," Ruth answered.
So she went down to the threshing floor and did everything her mother-in-law had told her.
When Boaz had finished eating and drinking and his heart was content, he went to lie down at the far end of the grain pile. Ruth came quietly, uncovered his feet, and lay down.
In the middle of the night the man was startled. He turned over, and there was a woman lying at his feet.
"Who are you?" he asked. "I am your servant Ruth," she said. "Spread the corner of your garment over your servant, for you are a redeemer."
Then he said, "The LORD bless you, my daughter. This last kindness of yours is greater than the first, for you have not gone after the young men, whether poor or rich.
And now, my daughter, do not be afraid. I will do for you all that you ask, for the whole town knows that you are a woman of noble character.
Now it is true that I am a redeemer, yet there is another redeemer more closely related than I.

versions.text: It is true that I am a redeemer, but there is a redeemer more closely related than I.
versions.explanation: The opening "And now" (וְעַתָּה) marks the turn in Boaz's speech and is dropped here; also "another redeemer" makes clearer that a second person is meant.

text: Stay here tonight. In the morning, if he will redeem you, good—let him redeem you. But if he is not willing, then as surely as the LORD lives, I will redeem you. Lie down until morning."
So she lay at his feet until morning, but she rose while it was still too dark for anyone to be recognized, for he had said, "No one must know that a woman came to the threshing floor."

versions.text: So she lay at his feet until morning, but she got up before anyone could recognize another; for he had said, "No one must know that a woman came to the threshing floor."
versions.explanation: "before anyone could recognize another" is awkward when read aloud and slightly unclear ("another" has no antecedent). The Hebrew idiom means it was still too dark for people to be identified. The semicolon also interrupts the oral flow; a comma reads more smoothly.

text: He also said, "Bring the cloak you are wearing and hold it out." When she did, he measured out six measures of barley and lifted it onto her. Then he went into the town.
When Ruth came to her mother-in-law, Naomi asked, "How did it go, my daughter?" [footnote: Hebrew, "Who are you, my daughter?"] And she told her everything the man had done for her.

versions.text: When Ruth came to her mother-in-law, Naomi asked, "How did it go, my daughter?" And she told her everything the man had done for her.
versions.explanation: The rendering "How did it go" is a reasonable idiomatic reading, but it departs noticeably from the Hebrew wording; a brief footnote giving the literal sense would help readers who compare with other renderings.

text: She added, "He gave me these six measures of barley and said, 'Do not go back to your mother-in-law empty-handed.'"
Then Naomi said, "Wait, my daughter, until you learn how the matter turns out, for the man will not rest until he has settled it today."
